title: Modulated soft-pinning and compatibility annotations for community model onboarding
creator: Aisha Patel
description: This PRD clarifies requirements to introduce a 'soft-pin' onboarding flow and compatibility annotation model for community/open weights in the Model Catalog. Goal: allow experimental/unvetted variants to be discoverable and routable while preserving runtime stability, predictable fallback behavior, and clear operator visibility.
background: We frequently onboard community model variants that are valuable for customers but may not meet strict compatibility guarantees. Current binary pinning (pinned/unpinned) causes tension: either we over-restrict access and slow adoption, or we allow untested variants to break serving and rollouts. A modulated soft-pin + compatibility annotation approach gives us finer levers for safety, telemetry, and graceful degradation.
scope_included: Add new catalog metadata fields: pin_mode (hard|soft|unrestricted), compat_signals (list of tags), compat_score (0-100) and runtime_hints (list).
Console UI: intake form changes to allow model owners to select pin_mode and provide compat_notes and runtime_hints.
API contract update: /catalog/models POST/PUT accepts new fields and returns validation warnings if missing.

Runtime behavior: implement soft-pin semantics where the request router prefers a soft-pinned variant but can fallback to a stable pinned variant under latency/quality SLO breach or kernel incompatibility.
Telemetry: opt-in telemetry flag for community models to surface compatibility telemetry (OOMs, kernel failures, quantization mismatches).
Acceptance tests and canary rollout plan for the new loader and router changes.
Migration path: backfill pin_mode=unrestricted for existing models and allow owners to opt into soft-pin via UI or API.
scope_excluded: Major runtime kernel rewrites; this work will use existing kernel capability metadata and feature flags.
Automatic model re-training or quality remediation—out of scope.
Billing model changes for soft-pinned variants.
acceptance_criteria: Catalog schema accepts and persists pin_mode, compat_signals, compat_score, runtime_hints and telemetry_opt_in for any new model and existing models are backfilled to pin_mode=unrestricted.

Console intake UI exposes pin_mode with contextual help and records owner-provided compat_notes. On submit, UI displays non-blocking warnings when compat_score < 60 or mandatory runtime_hints missing.
Router honors pin_mode semantics: hard -> never auto-fallback to other variants; soft -> prefer but allow fallback on detected runtime compatibility or SLO triggers; unrestricted -> no preference.

When a soft-pinned variant fails kernel compatibility or causes >5% increase in token-latency or >2x error rate relative to baseline for a 5-minute window, router triggers automatic fallback to the selected stable variant and records an incident in the model's timeline.
Telemetry pipeline captures kernel-level failures, OOMs, and quantization warnings for telemetry_opt_in=true models and surfaces aggregated metrics in Console within 2 hours after ingest.
End-to-end tests covering: intake -> catalog persistence -> router selection logic -> fallback under synthetic incompatibility; tests run in CI and pass on the branch before merge.
Rollout performed behind a feature flag; 100% of traffic to soft-pin routing logic can be toggled per-tenant.
Documentation: updated onboarding doc and API changelog with examples for soft-pin use cases and recommended compat_score thresholds.
No security review blockers remain; KMS/secret access unchanged and telemetry data does not include model inputs/outputs by default.
success_metrics: Within 30 days of GA, at least 25% of newly onboarded community variants use soft-pin or runtime_hints.
Number of model-caused runtime incidents from community variants decreases by 40% due to automatic fallback compared to baseline month.
Operator time-to-detect (mean) for compatibility regressions reduces from >6 hours to <2 hours due to telemetry and automated incidents.
No increase in platform-wide latency P95 attributable to soft-pin routing beyond 1%.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): schema + API + unit tests behind feature flag (ENG).
Phase 1 (internal canary): enable soft-pin for internal tenant + telemetry opt-in; run synthetic kernel incompat tests (2 weeks).
Phase 2 (early customers): opt-in customers (sign up via Sales/SE) enabled; observe metrics for 2 weeks and iterate (product + eng).
Phase 3 (GA): console UI visible to all; default pin_mode for new community models is unrestricted; soft-pin available as opt-in setting.
Post-GA (30/60/90 days): analyze adoption, incident trends, and adjust recommended compat_score thresholds and defaults.
test_steps: 1) Create model via API with pin_mode=soft, compat_score=45, telemetry_opt_in=true and ensure catalog returns 201 and stored fields match.
2) Ingest synthetic request that triggers a kernel incompatibility in soft variant and assert that router falls back to the chosen stable variant within 10s and logs incident.
3) Simulate latency degradation (increase token-latency by >5%) on soft variant for a 5-minute window and assert fallback triggers and rollback recorded.
4) Validate Console shows compat_signals, compat_score, and recent incidents for the model and that help text links to onboarding doc.
5) Confirm telemetry pipeline surfaces aggregated kernel failure counts and quantization warnings in Console within 2 hours.
6) Run CI integration tests with feature flag enabled; required to pass before merge.
open_questions: Should compat_score be author-provided only, or should we compute an initial heuristic via automated profiling?
Do we enforce a minimum compat_signals set for soft-pin models (for example, 'quantized', 'requires-custom-kernel')?
What is the appropriate default behavior for existing customers with pinned variants when a new soft-pinned variant is added to a model group?
Do we surface soft-pin fallback events as user-facing incidents or keep them operator-only by default?
What privacy guardrails are required for telemetry_opt_in to ensure no customer data is shipped?
decisions: Use pin_mode values: hard, soft, unrestricted (decided 2026-03-06).
Telemetry for community models must be opt-in; aggregate metrics only and no raw inputs/outputs captured (decided 2026-03-07).
Fallback triggers: kernel incompatibility OR sustained latency/error SLO breach as defined in acceptance criteria (decided 2026-03-09).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Soft-pinned variants could still cause transient instability during rollout. Mitigation: feature flag per-tenant and automatic fallback with fast rollback and incident logging.
Risk: Owners may mislabel compat_score. Mitigation: show prominent guidance and add optional automated profiler later (tracked as follow-up).
Risk: Increased telemetry cost. Mitigation: telemetry_opt_in default=false and aggregated rollups only.
